LLM_description:
Situation:
Joint Task Force is operating along a contested corridor with multiple forward combat units reliant on daily resupply from rear-area depots. Main supply routes run through exposed valleys and constricted passes subject to indirect fire, IEDs, and ambush. Weather, damaged bridges, and civilian traffic further hinder movement windows. Convoy security, engineer route clearance, and overwatch assets are available but limited. Supply Depot Alpha, Supply Depot Bravo, and other rear nodes hold stocks; forward units such as Falcon Battalion and Blackhorse Squadron require assured throughput to maintain tempo.

Mission:
Deliver assigned supplies from designated depots to all forward units across the planning horizon while maintaining combat power and minimizing total operational cost. Cost elements include transport, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment, and fixed route security risk costs associated with activating movement corridors.

Execution/Concept:
- Direct shipments will be planned from each depot to each unit for each day. Issues from any depot will not exceed available stock. Each unit’s daily requirement must be met by delivered flow or, if necessary, controlled shortfall; any unmet demand incurs a penalty.
- Vehicles are a constrained resource. Each vehicle has a fixed capacity, and the total deployed across all routes on a given day cannot exceed the fleet. Loads are measured against volumetric supply characteristics to ensure no vehicle exceeds capacity.
- Corridors between depots and units must be explicitly activated before use. Activating a route—sending any vehicles along it—incurs a fixed risk cost for that day to account for escort teams, route clearance, and overwatch, regardless of the number of vehicles sent. Vehicles may only travel on routes that have been activated.
- Approach: consolidate loads to reduce the number of activated routes; favor lower-risk corridors; source from nearer or better-stocked depots to limit transport burden; stage deliveries across days to stay within fleet limits; accept controlled shortfalls only where penalties are lower than the sum of transport, vehicle, and route risk costs.
- Risk and control measures: convoy movement will be scheduled inside secure windows; engineer and EOD teams will clear and mark routes; MPs will provide escort; patterns will vary to reduce predictability. Alternate corridors and depot retasking plans are prepared in case a primary route becomes non-permissive.
- Coordination: depots confirm issue capacity daily; units report updated priorities and consumption; movement control deconflicts convoys; fires and ISR support overwatch for high-risk segments.
